Mauricio Pochettino at Man Utd: Seven years on from the sack at Spurs what sort of coach is he now? We will soon find out
Seven years on from being sacked by Tottenham Hotspur, Mauricio Pochettino is back in the Premier League with Manchester United with an impressive reputation but a point to prove. Adam Bate asks whether he can roll back the years and deliver at Old Trafford...
Thursday 19 November 2026 09:53, UK
What Mauricio Pochettino achieved with Tottenham Hotspur in the previous decade looks even more impressive now than it did at the time. Manchester United really should have turned to the popular Argentine coach years ago.
In his five full seasons in charge, Spurs were in the Premier League's top five each time - a run that has never been bettered in their history. He took the club above Arsenal for the first time in a generation and into a Champions League final for the first time ever.
Silverware was missing, much to the amusement of his critics, but the charges against Manchester City serve as a reminder that he was playing with the deck stacked against him. He overachieved and it is his thrilling football that endures in the memory.
The arc of history has bent towards his intense style of play.

He is an obvious upgrade for Manchester United, a club that lurched from one error to the next but somehow appointed only one manager with Premier League experience in over a decade - and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's brief time at Cardiff hardly merited the job.
And yet, Pochettino, for all his undoubted charm - something that has helped to earn him so many vocal admirers in the media - still comes with a question mark. There is a point to prove here because that time at Tottenham ended exactly seven years ago.
In football, that is an age.
Jose Mourinho and Louis van Gaal have since been characterised as yesterday's men even upon their arrival, the former somewhat incongruously so now given that he is currently being deployed back on the bench at a little known outfit called Real Madrid.
But Mourinho came to United two years on from a Premier League title. For Van Gaal it would be his final club job. And yet, even he was fresh from a rather better World Cup and had taken Bayern Munich to a Champions League final four years prior not seven.
Pochettino has hardly been thumb twiddling in that time. There was a title win with Paris Saint-Germain, albeit at the second attempt. Some talk up his work with the United States. Others see particular parallels in how he navigated a tricky situation at Chelsea.
That chaos could prepare him well for his new assignment.
There is an argument that rather than his football ideas being compromised by these various challenges, he is a more rounded coach as a result. Player power will hardly be new to a man who had to field a front line of Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappe and Neymar.
Try getting those three to press the opposition.
Nevertheless, it is his accomplishments in constructing that Tottenham team that give the greatest cause for excitement. Can he build a side like that again? Does he even want to given that the Pochettino stamp has been less evident in his subsequent work?
In those first six seasons as a Premier League manager, Pochettino's teams never ranked lower than third for PPDA, the recognised metric for pressing. His Tottenham were pressing monsters, just as Espanyol and Southampton had been before that.
In his final four full seasons at Spurs, his sides never ranked lower than third for distance covered either. But his Chelsea team ranked among the bottom three on the same metric. It is indicative of how he has had to find a different way to get results.
That will certainly be the case at United, at least initially. He inherits a group of players ill-suited to the football that made him famous. As Pochettino's predecessor put it so memorably: "If you don't run forward and you don't run back, you aren't going to win."
The good news is that his reputation should buy him some time and trust. Enough for Pochettino's ideas to emerge. He has not done two years in a club job since Spurs and is now clutching a contract that should keep him at Manchester United until the summer of 2029.
Patience will be needed. One recalls one of his final interviews with Sky Sports during that time in charge of Tottenham, when the tempo began to slow and the vibrancy of his football lost some of its lustre. Those words seem just as relevant to the United of today.
"With a team that plays in the Champions League, a team in which 90 per cent of the players play for their national sides, it is important to remember how important pre-seasons are," he told Sky Sports. "This year, we did not have the stability and we started working late."
It is worth remembering that before he built that dynamic Spurs side led by Harry Kane, he had to chip away to construct the team. In that first season, he called on Federico Fazio and Vlad Chiriches, Etienne Capoue and Paulinho, Roberto Soldado and Emmanuel Adebayor.
At United, the turnaround in personnel and fortunes will need to be even greater. It is a mammoth task but this could still be the job of his life, even if Pochettino is already a decade older than Sir Alex Ferguson was when he arrived. Maybe they are made for each other...
Club and coach are looking to roll back the years.

מאוריציו פוצ'טינו חוזר לפרמייר ליג ומתמנה למאמן מנצ'סטר יונייטד, שבע שנים לאחר פטוריו מטוטנהאם הוטספור. תקופתו הקודמת בטוטנהאם כללה חמש עונות רצופות בצמרת הגבוהה והעפלה היסטורית לגמר ליגת האלופות, הישגים שמקבלים משנה תוקף במבט לאחור לנוכח האתגרים שעמדו בפניו.

מאז אותה תקופה עבר פוצ'טינו בפריז סן ז'רמן, שם זכה באליפות, וניהל את נבחרת ארצות הברית ואת צ'לסי. למרות המוניטין החיובי והכדורגל ההתקפי שהזדהה עמו בעבר, קיימים סימני שאלה סביב יכולתו להתאים את סגנון הלחץ המאפיין אותו למציאות הנוכחית של מנצ'סטר יונייטד, שנמצאת במצב המדורש לשינוי עמוק בסגל ובשיטות העבודה.

החוזה החדש של פוצ'טינו במועדון אמור להחזיק אותה בתפקיד עד קיץ 2029, תוך צורך בסבלנות מצד הנהלה והאוהדים כדי לבנות מחדש את הקבוצה ולהחזיר אותה למאבק על התארים הגבוהים.
